title: Caponata
subtitle: Sicilian sweet and sour aubergine stew
excerpt: Caponata is a Sicilian sweet and sour stew of fried aubergine, tomato, celery, olives, and capers finished with red wine vinegar and a little sugar. It is served cold or at room temperature as an antipasto. The sweet-sour balance is the defining characteristic and should be distinct rather than muted.
sourceNotes: Caponata is one of Sicily's most documented preparations, with origins traced to the Arabic influence on Sicilian cooking brought during the Arab rule of Sicily from the 9th to 11th centuries. The sweet and sour combination (agrodolce) is a characteristic of Sicilian cooking that appears in many contexts. Caponata is found in all of Sicily's major cities, with regional variations in Palermo, Catania, and Trapani. It appears in Italian cookbooks from the 19th century onward.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and improves after the first day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make at least 1 hour before serving. Caponata is much better the day after it is made, once the sweet-sour flavours have had time to mellow and combine.

glossaryTerms.definition: The Italian sweet and sour flavour principle, achieved by combining vinegar and sugar or honey in a dish. Used in caponata, rabbit, and some meat braises.

, comes from red wine vinegar and sugar added at the end of cooking. This should be a clear flavour rather than a faint background note. Caponata is always served cold or at room temperature as an antipasto, and it is always better the day after it is made.

items.prepNote: plus extra for frying the aubergine

content.text: Season the aubergine cubes with salt and leave in a colander for 20 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.
Fry the aubergine in batches in a large frying pan with generous olive oil over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and soft. Drain on kitchen paper and set aside.
In a separate pan, fry the onion in 3 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add the celery and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes, crushing them into the pan. Cook for 10 minutes over medium heat until the sauce is thick.

Add the olives, capers, and fried aubergine. Stir to combine. Add the red wine vinegar and sugar. Cook for 5 more minutes, stirring. Taste: the sweet-sour balance should be clear. Adjust with more vinegar or sugar.
Remove from the heat and cool completely. Serve at room temperature, drizzled with a little extra olive oil.

Caponata is from Sicily. The sweet-sour flavour in Sicilian cooking comes from Arab influence, brought to the island between the 9th and 11th centuries. Each Sicilian city makes it differently: the Palermo version uses celery, Catania adds dark chocolate, Trapani adds almonds. The version here follows the Palermo style, which is the most common.
